records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: "The word of the LORD came to me, saying" keeps the wording set for Jeremiah at each level, here and at verses 17 and 23. The chapter has three messages against Jerusalem: its crimes (verses 1-16), the furnace (17-22), and the failure of every group of its leaders and people (23-31).

records.heading: The city of bloodshed

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם הֲתִשְׁפֹּ֥ט הֲתִשְׁפֹּ֖ט אֶת־עִ֣יר הַדָּמִ֑ים וְה֣וֹדַעְתָּ֔הּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then make known to her all her abominations.
pieces: As for you, son of man, will you judge? Will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then confront her with all her detestable practices.

L.2: And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then make known to her all her abominations.

R.2: Son of man, are you ready to judge? Will you judge this city that is guilty of murder? Then show her all the disgusting things she has done.

decisions.choice: will you judge?: a call to bring the charge, in effect a command
decisions.reason: As in 20:4, the repeated question tells the prophet to state the case against the city, and the command that follows says how.

decisions.choice: the city of bloodshed: a city guilty of shedding blood
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "the city of bloods", a plural that means bloodshed and the guilt it brings. Nahum 3:1 calls Nineveh the same, and Ezekiel uses it again of Jerusalem in 24:6 and 9. The blood is murder and violence, including the deaths caused by injustice and child sacrifice (verses 6-12; 16:20-21).

decisions.choice: this city that is guilty of murder
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name means (m2). Jerusalem is "her", as the city is pictured as a woman throughout the chapter.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה עִ֣יר שֹׁפֶ֥כֶת דָּ֛ם בְּתוֹכָ֖הּ לָב֣וֹא עִתָּ֑הּ וְעָשְׂתָ֧ה גִלּוּלִ֛ים עָלֶ֖יהָ לְטָמְאָֽה׃
records.gloss: And say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: A city shedding blood in her midst, for coming of her time, and [that] makes idols for herself, for defiling!
pieces: Say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: A city that sheds blood within her walls and so brings on her time of doom, that makes idols for herself and so defiles herself!

L.3: And say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: A city shedding blood in her midst, so that her time comes, and that makes filthy idols for herself, to defile herself!

R.3: Say, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: This city kills people inside its walls, and so it brings its own time of judgment closer. It makes idols for itself, and they make it unclean.

decisions.choice: her time: the time of her judgment
decisions.reason: "Time" here is the appointed time of punishment, as in 7:7, 12 and 21:30. By her own acts the city brings it nearer.

decisions.choice: bloodshed and idols: the two charges of the chapter
decisions.reason: Ezekiel brings the two together again and again: wrongs against people (blood) and wrongs against God (idols). Both make the city unclean, and both bring judgment (verse 4; 36:18).

decisions.choice: kills people
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what shedding blood means, and calls the city "it", which is clearer in plain English. Verse 4 then speaks to the city as "you", as the Hebrew does.

records.source: בְּדָמֵ֨ךְ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁפַ֜כְתְּ אָשַׁ֗מְתְּ וּבְגִלּוּלַ֤יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂית֙ טָמֵ֔את וַתַּקְרִ֣יבִי יָמַ֔יִךְ וַתָּב֖וֹא עַד־שְׁנוֹתָ֑יִךְ עַל־כֵּ֗ן נְתַתִּ֤יךְ חֶרְפָּה֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְקַלָּסָ֖ה לְכָל־הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: By your blood that you have shed you have become guilty, and by your idols that you have made you have become defiled, and you have brought near your days and come to your years. Therefore I have made you a disgrace among the nations and an object of mockery to all the lands.
pieces: You have become guilty by the blood you have shed, and made unclean by the idols you have made. You have hastened your days and come to the end of your years. So I have made you an object of scorn to the nations and a laughingstock to all the countries.

L.4: By your blood that you have shed you have become guilty, and by your filthy idols that you have made you have become defiled; and you have brought near your days, and you have come to your years. Therefore I have made you a disgrace among the nations and an object of mockery to all the lands.

R.4: You are guilty because you have murdered people. You are unclean because you have made idols. You have brought your end closer, and the end of your life has come. So I have made you something the nations scorn. All the countries make fun of you.

decisions.choice: brought near your days, come to your years: brought on the end of your life
decisions.reason: The days and years are the city's lifetime, which is now running out. Her crimes have hastened the day of judgment (verse 3).

decisions.choice: a reproach to the nations and a mockery: a ruin that others scorn
decisions.reason: This is the curse that the law warns of (Deuteronomy 28:37) and that 5:14-15 already threatened against Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: brought your end closer; the end of your life has come
alternatives: brought near your days; come to your years
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

records.source: הַקְּרֹב֛וֹת וְהָרְחֹק֥וֹת מִמֵּ֖ךְ יִתְקַלְּסוּ־בָ֑ךְ טְמֵאַ֣ת הַשֵּׁ֔ם רַבַּ֖ת הַמְּהוּמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Those near and those far from you will mock you, defiled of name, full of turmoil.
pieces: Those who are near and those who are far away will mock you, you city with a stained name, full of turmoil.

L.5: Those near and those far from you will mock you, [you] defiled of name, full of turmoil.

R.5: People who live near you and people far away will make fun of you. Your name is ruined, and you are full of disorder.

decisions.choice: defiled of name: a city whose reputation is stained
decisions.reason: The name is the city's reputation. Jerusalem, which bore God's name (1 Kings 11:36), is now known for its uncleanness.

decisions.choice: full of turmoil: full of disorder and panic
decisions.reason: The word is used of confusion and unrest in a society (Amos 3:9) and of the panic God sends on his enemies (Deuteronomy 7:23). Both senses fit a city torn by violence.

records.source: הִנֵּה֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֥ישׁ לִזְרֹע֖וֹ הָ֣יוּ בָ֑ךְ לְמַ֖עַן שְׁפָךְ־דָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Behold, [the] princes of Israel, each according to his arm, have been in you, in order to shed blood.
pieces: Look at the princes of Israel within you: each of them uses his power to shed blood.

L.6: See, the princes of Israel, each according to his arm, have been in you to shed blood.

R.6: Look at the rulers of Israel who live in you. Each of them uses his power to kill people.

decisions.choice: each according to his arm: each by the power he had
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength. Each ruler used his power for violence instead of justice.

decisions.choice: the princes of Israel: the kings of Judah and their royal house
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses "prince" for Israel's kings (12:10; 21:30). The books of Kings and Jeremiah charge kings of Judah with shedding innocent blood: Manasseh filled Jerusalem with it (2 Kings 21:16; 24:4), and Jehoiakim's eyes and heart were set on shedding it (Jeremiah 22:17).

decisions.choice: rulers
decisions.reason: The word for prince is "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruler" at Readable, as set for Ezekiel.

records.source: אָ֤ב וָאֵם֙ הֵקַ֣לּוּ בָ֔ךְ לַגֵּ֛ר עָשׂ֥וּ בַעֹ֖שֶׁק בְּתוֹכֵ֑ךְ יָת֥וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֖ה ה֥וֹנוּ בָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Father and mother they have treated with contempt in you; toward the sojourner they have acted with oppression in your midst; orphan and widow they have wronged in you.
pieces: In you, father and mother are treated with contempt; in your midst the foreigner is oppressed; in you the orphan and the widow are wronged.

L.7: Father and mother they have treated with contempt in you; with the sojourner they have dealt by oppression in your midst; the fatherless and the widow they have wronged in you.

R.7: People in you do not respect their fathers and mothers. They oppress foreigners who live among them. They mistreat orphans and widows.

decisions.choice: the commands of the law, broken one by one
decisions.reason: The list in verses 7-12 follows the laws of Leviticus 18-20 and Exodus 20-23: honor father and mother (Exodus 20:12; Leviticus 19:3), do not wrong the foreigner (Exodus 22:20; Leviticus 19:33-34), do not mistreat the widow or the fatherless (Exodus 22:21-23). Deuteronomy 27:16-19 puts curses on the same acts.

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a foreigner living in Israel without land or family there
decisions.reason: Such people, like orphans and widows, had no one to protect them, and the law put them under God's special care.

decisions.choice: sojourner (L); foreigner (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows Exodus 22:20, as published. Balanced puts the three clauses in the passive, which keeps the Hebrew's stress on the victims.

records.source: קָדָשַׁ֖י בָּזִ֑ית וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתֹתַ֖י חִלָּֽלְתְּ׃
records.gloss: My holy things you have despised, and my sabbaths you have profaned.
pieces: You have despised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things and dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths.

L.8: My holy things you have despised, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths you have profaned.

R.8: You have treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things with scorn. You have treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days with no respect.

decisions.choice: my holy things: everything set apart for God: offerings, the sanctuary and what belongs to it
decisions.reason: Leviticus 19:8 and 22:2 warn against profaning the LORD's holy things. Verse 26 charges the priests with the same sin.

decisions.choice: profaning the Sabbaths: as in 20:13
decisions.reason: The Sabbath was the sign of the covenant (20:12), and profaning it is named again here and in verse 26.

records.source: אַנְשֵׁ֥י רָכִ֛יל הָ֥יוּ בָ֖ךְ לְמַ֣עַן שְׁפָךְ־דָּ֑ם וְאֶל־הֶֽהָרִים֙ אָ֣כְלוּ בָ֔ךְ זִמָּ֖ה עָשׂ֥וּ בְתוֹכֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Men of slander have been in you in order to shed blood; and on the mountains they have eaten in you; lewdness they have done in your midst.
pieces: In you are slanderers who are out to shed blood. In you are those who eat at the mountain shrines. In your midst they commit depraved acts.

L.9: Men of slander have been in you, in order to shed blood; and on the mountains they have eaten in you; lewdness they have committed in your midst.

R.9: Some of your people tell lies about others so that they will be put to death. Some eat sacrifices to idols at the shrines on the mountains. Others do shameful things.

decisions.choice: slanderers who shed blood: false accusers who bring about the death of others
decisions.reason: Leviticus 19:16 puts the two together: "Do not go about as a slanderer among your people; do not stand against the blood of your neighbor." The false witnesses against Naboth are an example (1 Kings 21:10-13).

decisions.choice: eating on the mountains: sacrificial meals at the hill shrines
decisions.reason: To "eat on the mountains" is to share in the feasts held at idol shrines on the hills (18:6, 11, 15).

decisions.choice: lewdness: shameful, depraved acts, especially sexual sins
decisions.reason: The word is used for sexual wrongs in Leviticus 18:17 and 20:14, and it leads into the list of verses 10-11.

decisions.choice: slanderers (B); people who tell lies about others (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "men of"; Balanced and Readable use words that name the act, which applies to anyone who does it. Readable adds "sacrifices to idols" to say what the eating means (m2).

records.source: עֶרְוַת־אָ֖ב גִּלָּה־בָ֑ךְ טְמֵאַ֥ת הַנִּדָּ֖ה עִנּוּ־בָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of a father they uncover in you; [a woman] unclean in impurity they violate in you.
pieces: In you men have sexual relations with their father's wife; in you they violate women who are unclean during their monthly period.

L.10: In you they uncover [their] father's nakedness; in you they violate [a woman who is] unclean in [her] impurity.

R.10: In you men have sexual relations with their fathers' wives. They violate women during their monthly periods, when the women are unclean.

decisions.choice: uncover a father's nakedness: have sexual relations with one's father's wife
decisions.reason: This is the language of the law. Leviticus 18:7-8 and 20:11 forbid a man to have relations with his father's wife, "the nakedness of your father".

decisions.choice: a woman unclean in her impurity: a woman during her monthly period
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:19 and 20:18 forbid sexual relations during a woman's monthly period, while she is ritually unclean.

decisions.choice: violate: humiliate sexually, often by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble or humiliate. It is used for rape (Genesis 34:2; 2 Samuel 13:12-14) and for relations that shame a woman (Deuteronomy 22:24, 29). Here it stresses the wrong done to the woman.

decisions.choice: plain and sober wording: "have sexual relations with their father's wife"; "violate"
decisions.reason: As the book's register rule says for these passages, Literal follows the Hebrew and Balanced and Readable state the meaning plainly, neither blurring it nor adding detail. The wording follows Leviticus 18:8 and 18:19, as published.

records.source: וְאִ֣ישׁ׀אֶת־אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֗הוּ עָשָׂה֙ תּֽוֹעֵבָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־כַּלָּת֖וֹ טִמֵּ֣א בְזִמָּ֑ה וְאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־אֲחֹת֥וֹ בַת־אָבִ֖יו עִנָּה־בָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And a man with [the] wife of his neighbor commits abomination, and a man his daughter-in-law defiles with lewdness, and a man his sister, [the] daughter of his father, violates in you.
pieces: One man commits a detestable act with his neighbor's wife; another shamefully defiles his daughter-in-law; and another in you violates his sister, his own father's daughter.

L.11: And a man commits an abomination with his neighbor's wife, and a man defiles his daughter-in-law with lewdness, and a man in you violates his sister, his father's daughter.

R.11: One man does a disgusting thing with his neighbor's wife. Another has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law and so makes her unclean. Another violates his own sister, his father's daughter.

decisions.choice: adultery, a daughter-in-law, a half-sister: the laws of Leviticus 18 and 20
decisions.reason: Leviticus forbids relations with a neighbor's wife (18:20; 20:10), with a daughter-in-law (18:15; 20:12) and with a sister, "your father's daughter" (18:9; 20:17). Ezekiel names each as done in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: abomination: an act the LORD finds detestable
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the sexual sins of Leviticus 18:26-30.

decisions.choice: plain and sober wording
decisions.reason: The register rule applies: the meaning is stated plainly, without crude or added detail. The book's wording for the word "abomination" is kept: "abomination" (L), "detestable act" (B), "disgusting thing" (R).

records.source: שֹׁ֥חַד לָֽקְחוּ־בָ֖ךְ לְמַ֣עַן שְׁפָךְ־דָּ֑ם נֶ֧שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּ֣ית לָקַ֗חַתְּ וַתְּבַצְּעִ֤י רֵעַ֨יִךְ֙ בַּעֹ֔שֶׁק וְאֹתִ֣י שָׁכַ֔חַתְּ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: A bribe they take in you in order to shed blood; interest and increase you take, and you make gain of your neighbors by extortion, and me you have forgotten, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: In you people take bribes to shed blood. You charge interest and take profit, you make gain from your neighbors by extortion, and you have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: Bribes they take in you, in order to shed blood; interest and profit you take, and you make gain of your neighbors by oppression; and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you have forgotten, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: People in you take money to have others killed. You charge interest and make a profit from loans. You cheat your neighbors to get rich. And you have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: bribes to shed blood
decisions.reason: The law curses anyone who "takes a bribe to strike down an innocent person" (Deuteronomy 27:25; compare Exodus 23:8).

decisions.choice: interest and profit: charging the poor for loans
decisions.reason: The law forbade charging interest or taking profit on a loan to a fellow Israelite in need (Exodus 22:24; Leviticus 25:36-37). Ezekiel 18:8, 13 and 17 count it among the marks of a wicked person.

decisions.choice: you have forgotten me: the root of the other sins
decisions.reason: Forgetting the LORD is the warning of Deuteronomy 8:11-14 and the charge of Jeremiah 2:32 and Hosea 13:6. The list of wrongs ends with the one that explains them all.

records.source: וְהִנֵּה֙ הִכֵּ֣יתִי כַפִּ֔י אֶל־בִּצְעֵ֖ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑ית וְעַ֨ל־דָּמֵ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בְּתוֹכֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And behold, I strike my hand at your unjust gain that you have made, and at your blood that has been in your midst.
pieces: Look, I strike {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands together at the dishonest gain you have made and at the bloodshed in your midst.

L.13: And see, I strike {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand at your unjust gain that you have made, and at your blood that has been in your midst.

R.13: I clap {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands in anger at the money you have gained dishonestly and at the murders done in you.

decisions.choice: strike my hand: a gesture of anger and scorn
decisions.reason: God makes the same gesture over the sword in 21:22, and the prophet in 6:11 and 21:19.

decisions.choice: in anger
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture means (m1).

records.source: הֲיַעֲמֹ֤ד לִבֵּךְ֙ אִם־תֶּחֱזַ֣קְנָה יָדַ֔יִךְ לַיָּמִ֕ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י עֹשֶׂ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ךְ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִֽׂיתִי׃
records.gloss: Will endure your heart, or will be strong your hands, in the days that I [am] dealing with you? I, Yahweh, have spoken and will act.
pieces: Will your courage hold, or your hands stay strong, in the days when I take action against you? I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do it.

L.14: Will your heart endure, or will your hands be strong, in the days when I am dealing with you? I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will act.

R.14: Will you still be brave? Will you be strong enough when I punish you? I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do what I have said.

decisions.choice: will your heart endure, will your hands be strong?: will you have the courage and strength to bear it?
decisions.reason: The heart stands for courage and the hands for strength (compare 7:17; 21:12). The question expects the answer "no".

decisions.choice: I have spoken and I will act: God's word and his deed go together
decisions.reason: The same words close 17:24 and 36:36.

records.source: וַהֲפִיצוֹתִ֤י אוֹתָךְ֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְזֵרִיתִ֖יךְ בָּאֲרָצ֑וֹת וַהֲתִמֹּתִ֥י טֻמְאָתֵ֖ךְ מִמֵּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you in the lands, and I will consume your uncleanness from you.
pieces: I will scatter you among the nations, spread you through the countries and burn away your uncleanness.

L.15: And I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you in the lands, and I will consume your uncleanness out of you.

R.15: I will scatter you among the nations and spread you out through other countries. I will remove everything that makes you unclean.

decisions.choice: I will consume your uncleanness: the exile will put an end to it
decisions.reason: The verb means to finish or bring to an end. The scattering is punishment, but it also does away with the city's uncleanness, as the furnace of verses 17-22 pictures.

decisions.choice: scatter and disperse: the oath of the wilderness carried out
decisions.reason: The same words were used of God's oath in the wilderness (20:23).

records.source: וְנִחַ֥לְתְּ בָּ֖ךְ לְעֵינֵ֣י גוֹיִ֑ם וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And you will be profaned through yourself in [the] eyes of [the] nations, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Because of your own doing you will be dishonored before the nations. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: And you will be profaned through yourself in the eyes of the nations, and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: You will be disgraced in front of the nations because of what you have done. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you will be profaned through yourself: the Hebrew text
alternatives: "I will take possession of you" (the Septuagint, reading a verb from the same letters)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew means that Jerusalem's own acts will bring her dishonor before the nations. The Greek seems to read the same letters as a different verb, "I will take you as an inheritance", and some read "I will be profaned", as God's name is profaned among the nations in 20:9 and 36:20. The Hebrew makes sense and is followed.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD: the book's refrain
decisions.reason: See the note at 6:7.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.17: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: A new message begins: the furnace (verses 18-22).

records.heading: Dross in the furnace

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הָיוּ־לִ֥י בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְסִ֑יג כֻּלָּ֡ם נְ֠חֹשֶׁת וּבְדִ֨יל וּבַרְזֶ֤ל וְעוֹפֶ֨רֶת֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ כּ֔וּר סִגִ֥ים כֶּ֖סֶף הָיֽוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Son of man, have become to me [the] house of Israel dross; all of them [are] bronze and tin and iron and lead in [the] midst of a furnace; dross of silver they have become.
pieces: Son of man, in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight the house of Israel has become dross. All of them are bronze, tin, iron and lead left in the furnace; they have become the dross from silver.

L.18: Son of man, the house of Israel has become to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dross; all of them [are] bronze and tin and iron and lead in the middle of a furnace; they have become the dross of silver.

R.18: Son of man, the people of Israel have become like worthless slag to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are like the bronze, tin, iron and lead left in a furnace. They are only the waste left over when silver is refined.

decisions.choice: dross: the waste left when silver is refined
decisions.reason: Silver was refined by melting the ore with lead in a furnace; the other metals and impurities were drawn off as dross and the pure silver was left. Isaiah 1:22, 25 and Jeremiah 6:28-30 use the same picture for Israel.

decisions.choice: dross of silver: nothing of value is left
alternatives: a picture of purifying, which leaves pure silver at the end (Isaiah 1:25; Malachi 3:3)
decisions.reason: In Isaiah and Malachi the furnace refines and something precious remains. Here the people are all dross; the furnace of verses 19-22 is a picture of judgment, and no pure silver is mentioned.

decisions.choice: worthless slag; the waste left over when silver is refined
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "dross" (m1).

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֛עַן הֱי֥וֹת כֻּלְּכֶ֖ם לְסִגִ֑ים לָכֵן֙ הִנְנִ֣י קֹבֵ֣ץ אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־תּ֖וֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because all of you have become dross, therefore behold, I [am] gathering you into [the] midst of Jerusalem.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Because all of you have become dross, I am about to gather you into Jerusalem.

L.19: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because all of you have become dross, therefore see, I am gathering you into the midst of Jerusalem.

R.19: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: All of you have become like worthless slag. So I am going to gather you into Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: gathered into Jerusalem: the people crowd into the city as the enemy comes
decisions.reason: When an army invaded, people from the countryside fled into the walled city (Jeremiah 4:5; 35:11). The city they trusted to protect them becomes the furnace.

records.source: קְבֻ֣צַת כֶּ֡סֶף וּ֠נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶ֨ל וְעוֹפֶ֤רֶת וּבְדִיל֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ כּ֔וּר לָפַֽחַת־עָלָ֥יו אֵ֖שׁ לְהַנְתִּ֑יךְ כֵּ֤ן אֶקְבֹּץ֙ בְּאַפִּ֣י וּבַחֲמָתִ֔י וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י וְהִתַּכְתִּ֖י אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: [As] a gathering of silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into [the] middle of a furnace, to blow on it fire to melt [it], so I will gather in my anger and in my wrath, and I will put [you in] and melt you.
pieces: As silver, bronze, iron, lead and tin are gathered into a furnace and fire is blown on them to melt them, so I will gather you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, put you in and melt you.

L.20: As [one] gathers silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into the middle of a furnace, to blow fire upon it for melting, so in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath I will gather [you], and I will put [you in] and melt you.

R.20: People put silver, bronze, iron, lead and tin into a furnace. They blow on the fire to make it hot enough to melt the metals. In the same way I will gather you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great anger. I will put you into the fire and melt you.

decisions.choice: blowing on the fire: with bellows, to make the furnace hot
decisions.reason: A smith blew air into the fire with bellows to raise the heat (Jeremiah 6:29). In verse 21 God himself blows with the fire of his wrath.

decisions.choice: I will put you in: or "I will leave you there"
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to set down or to leave. Here it most likely means placing the metal in the furnace.

records.source: וְכִנַּסְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְנָפַחְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּאֵ֣שׁ עֶבְרָתִ֑י וְנִתַּכְתֶּ֖ם בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And I will gather you and blow on you with [the] fire of my wrath, and you will be melted in its midst.
pieces: I will gather you and blow the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you, and you will melt inside the city.

L.21: And I will gather you, and I will blow on you with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath; and in its midst you will melt.

R.21: I will gather you and blow on you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fiery anger, and you will melt inside the city.

decisions.choice: in its midst: inside Jerusalem, which is the furnace
decisions.reason: "Its" is feminine and refers back to Jerusalem (verse 19), the place of the melting.

decisions.choice: inside the city
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the city (m1).

records.source: כְּהִתּ֥וּךְ כֶּ֨סֶף֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ כּ֔וּר כֵּ֖ן תֻּתְּכ֣וּ בְתוֹכָ֑הּ וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה שָׁפַ֥כְתִּי חֲמָתִ֖י עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: As silver is melted in [the] midst of a furnace, so you will be melted in its midst; and you will know that I, Yahweh, have poured out my wrath on you.
pieces: As silver melts in a furnace, so you will melt inside the city. Then you will know that it is I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you.

L.22: As silver is melted in the middle of a furnace, so you will be melted in its midst; and you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you.

R.22: Just as silver melts in a furnace, you will melt inside the city. Then you will know that it is I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you.

decisions.choice: you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out my wrath: the refrain, extended
decisions.reason: The refrain "you will know that I am the LORD" here says what they will know: that the disaster is the LORD's own judgment.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.23: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: A new message begins: every group in the land has failed (verses 24-31).

records.heading: No one to stand in the gap

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֱמָר־לָ֕הּ אַ֣תְּ אֶ֔רֶץ לֹ֥א מְטֹהָרָ֖ה הִ֑יא לֹ֥א גֻשְׁמָ֖הּ בְּי֥וֹם זָֽעַם׃
records.gloss: Son of man, say to her, You [are] a land not cleansed, not rained upon in [the] day of indignation.
pieces: Son of man, say to the land, You are a land that has not been cleansed, that has had no rain on the day of wrath.

L.24: Son of man, say to her, You [are] a land that is not cleansed, not rained upon in the day of indignation.

R.24: Son of man, speak to the land of Israel. Tell it, You are a land that has not been made clean. No rain has fallen on you on the day of anger.

decisions.choice: not cleansed: the Hebrew text
alternatives: "not rained upon" (the Septuagint, which has the same word in both halves of the verse)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "not cleansed" and then "not rained upon"; the Greek has "not rained upon" in the first half too. The Hebrew pairs the two pictures: a land that has not been washed clean and has had no rain.

decisions.choice: no rain on the day of wrath: rain withheld as a sign of judgment
decisions.reason: Rain was a sign of God's blessing, and drought of his anger (Deuteronomy 11:13-17; Jeremiah 3:3; Amos 4:7). The land is both unwashed and unblessed.

decisions.choice: the land; the land of Israel
decisions.reason: "Her" in Hebrew is the land, as the rest of the verse shows; Balanced and Readable name it.

records.source: קֶ֤שֶׁר נְבִיאֶ֨יהָ֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ כַּאֲרִ֥י שׁוֹאֵ֖ג טֹ֣רֵֽף טָ֑רֶף נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָכָ֗לוּ חֹ֤סֶן וִיקָר֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ אַלְמְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ הִרְבּ֥וּ בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: A conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a lion roaring, tearing prey; lives they have devoured; treasure and precious things they take; her widows they have made many in her midst.
pieces: Her prophets within her have joined in a conspiracy. Like a roaring lion tearing its prey, they devour people; they seize treasure and precious things and make many widows in the land.

L.25: [There is] a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing prey; they have devoured lives; treasure and precious things they take; her widows they have multiplied in her midst.

R.25: Her prophets have joined together in an evil plan. They are like a roaring lion tearing its prey. They destroy people's lives. They take treasure and valuable things. Because of them, many women in the land have become widows.

decisions.choice: a conspiracy of her prophets: the Hebrew text
alternatives: "whose princes in her midst are like a roaring lion" (the Septuagint, reading "her princes" for the very similar "her prophets")
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "her prophets" and "her princes" differ by one letter, and "conspiracy" and "who" are also close. The Greek reads "princes", which would fit the killing, plunder and widows of this verse and keep the prophets for verse 28. The Hebrew is followed, and it makes sense: prophets who took sides in the plots of the city (13:19; Jeremiah 23:9-14).

decisions.choice: like a roaring lion: Ezekiel's list follows Zephaniah 3:3-4
decisions.reason: Zephaniah describes Jerusalem's officials as roaring lions, its judges as wolves, its prophets as reckless and its priests as profaning what is holy and doing violence to the instruction. Ezekiel 22:25-28 takes up the same list, adding the people of the land (verse 29).

decisions.choice: in the land
decisions.reason: "Her" here is the land (verse 24). Readable says that the widows are the wives of those killed.

records.source: כֹּהֲנֶ֜יהָ חָמְס֣וּ תוֹרָתִי֮ וַיְחַלְּל֣וּ קָדָשַׁי֒ בֵּֽין־קֹ֤דֶשׁ לְחֹל֙ לֹ֣א הִבְדִּ֔ילוּ וּבֵין־הַטָּמֵ֥א לְטָה֖וֹר לֹ֣א הוֹדִ֑יעוּ וּמִשַׁבְּתוֹתַי֙ הֶעְלִ֣ימוּ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם וָאֵחַ֖ל בְּתוֹכָֽם׃
records.gloss: Her priests have done violence to my instruction and profaned my holy things; between holy and common they have not distinguished, and between the unclean and the clean they have not taught; and from my sabbaths they have hidden their eyes, and I am profaned in their midst.
pieces: Her priests do violence to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction and profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things. They do not separate the holy from the common, and do not teach the difference between the unclean and the clean. They shut their eyes to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths, and so I am dishonored among them.

L.26: Her priests have done violence to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction and profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things; between holy and common they have made no distinction, and between the unclean and the clean they have not taught [the difference]; and from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths they have hidden their eyes, and I am profaned among them.

R.26: Her priests twist {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching and treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things as common. They do not teach people the difference between what is holy and what is not, or between what is unclean and what is clean. They pay no attention to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days. So among them I am treated with no respect.

decisions.choice: holy and common, unclean and clean: the priests' own task, as Leviticus 10:10-11 sets it
decisions.reason: The priests were given the duty "to separate between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean, and to teach" the people (Leviticus 10:10-11). Ezekiel's future priests will do it (44:23). Zephaniah 3:4 also charges the priests with doing violence to the instruction.

decisions.choice: hidden their eyes from my Sabbaths: ignored them
decisions.reason: To hide one's eyes is to refuse to see (Leviticus 20:4; Isaiah 1:15).

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R)
decisions.reason: The word *torah* follows the wording settled for the prophets. The phrase "do violence to the instruction" keeps the wording of Zephaniah 3:4 at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: שָׂרֶ֣יהָ בְקִרְבָּ֔הּ כִּזְאֵבִ֖ים טֹ֣רְפֵי טָ֑רֶף לִשְׁפָּךְ־דָּם֙ לְאַבֵּ֣ד נְפָשׁ֔וֹת לְמַ֖עַן בְּצֹ֥עַ בָּֽצַע׃
records.gloss: Her officials in her midst [are] like wolves tearing prey, to shed blood, to destroy lives, in order to make unjust gain.
pieces: Her officials within her are like wolves tearing their prey. They shed blood and destroy lives to make dishonest gain.

L.27: Her officials in her midst [are] like wolves tearing prey, shedding blood, destroying lives, to make unjust gain.

R.27: Her leaders are like wolves tearing their prey. They kill people and destroy lives to get rich by cheating.

decisions.choice: officials like wolves: as Zephaniah 3:3
decisions.reason: Zephaniah calls the judges "wolves of the evening" and the officials "roaring lions". Ezekiel uses the lion for verse 25 and the wolf for the officials.

decisions.choice: officials (L, B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The word *sar* follows the wording settled for the prophets.

records.source: וּנְבִיאֶ֗יהָ טָח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ תָּפֵ֔ל חֹזִ֣ים שָׁ֔וְא וְקֹסְמִ֥ים לָהֶ֖ם כָּזָ֑ב אֹמְרִ֗ים כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וַֽיהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א דִבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And her prophets have smeared for them whitewash, seeing false [visions] and divining for them a lie, saying, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh, and Yahweh has not spoken.
pieces: Her prophets cover these deeds with whitewash. They see false visions and practice lying divination for them, saying, "The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this," when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not spoken.

L.28: And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, "Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}," when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not spoken.

R.28: Her prophets cover up these sins, as people cover a bad wall with whitewash. They see false visions and tell lies about the future. They say, "This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says," but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not spoken at all.

decisions.choice: smeared whitewash: the picture of 13:10-16
decisions.reason: In chapter 13 the false prophets cover a flimsy wall with whitewash, giving it a look of strength, and God's storm brings it down. Here the whitewash covers the crimes of the leaders.

decisions.choice: false visions, lying divination, "Thus says the Lord GOD": as 13:6-9
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses the same words for the prophets who speak in God's name without being sent (13:6-7; Jeremiah 23:16-32).

decisions.choice: cover up these sins, as people cover a bad wall with whitewash
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1). The prophets' words take quotation marks, since they are speech quoted inside the oracle.

records.source: עַ֤ם הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ עָ֣שְׁקוּ עֹ֔שֶׁק וְגָזְל֖וּ גָּזֵ֑ל וְעָנִ֤י וְאֶבְיוֹן֙ הוֹנ֔וּ וְאֶת־הַגֵּ֥ר עָשְׁק֖וּ בְּלֹ֥א מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: [The] people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery; and [the] poor and needy they have wronged; and the sojourner they have oppressed without justice.
pieces: The people of the land practice extortion and commit robbery. They wrong the poor and needy and oppress the foreigner, denying them justice.

L.29: The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery; and they have wronged the poor and needy, and they have oppressed the sojourner without justice.

R.29: Even the landowners cheat others and rob them. They mistreat poor and needy people. They oppress foreigners and do not treat them fairly.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the landowning citizens of Judah
alternatives: the common people as a whole
decisions.reason: In the last years of Judah, "the people of the land" were the free, landowning men who had a voice in public affairs, such as making a king (2 Kings 21:24; 23:30). Ezekiel names them after the rulers, priests, officials and prophets: no group is innocent.

decisions.choice: the poor, the needy and the sojourner: those the law protects
decisions.reason: See verse 7 and Exodus 22:20-26; Deuteronomy 24:14-15.

decisions.choice: the landowners
decisions.reason: Readable says who the people of the land were (m1), and adds "even", since they are the last group in the list.

records.source: וָאֲבַקֵּ֣שׁ מֵהֶ֡ם אִ֣ישׁ גֹּֽדֵר־גָּדֵר֩ וְעֹמֵ֨ד בַּפֶּ֧רֶץ לְפָנַ֛י בְּעַ֥ד הָאָ֖רֶץ לְבִלְתִּ֣י שַׁחֲתָ֑הּ וְלֹ֖א מָצָֽאתִי׃
records.gloss: And I sought among them a man building up a wall and standing in the breach before me on behalf of the land, so as not to destroy it; but I did not find [one].
pieces: I looked for {{gender:someone|a man}} among them who would repair the wall and stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the gap on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it, but I found no one.

L.30: And I sought among them {{gender:someone|a man}} who would build up a wall and stand in the breach before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it; but I did not find [one].

R.30: I looked for {{gender:someone|a man}} among them to build up the wall and to stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the broken place to protect the land, so that I would not destroy it. But I could not find anyone.

decisions.choice: build up a wall and stand in the breach: defend the city, here by turning God's anger away
decisions.reason: When an enemy broke through a wall, soldiers stood in the gap to hold it. In 13:5 the false prophets did not "go up into the breaches" or build up a wall. Psalm 106:23 says that Moses "stood in the breach before" God to turn away his wrath; that is the kind of person God looked for: someone whose righteousness and pleading would stand between the land and judgment.

decisions.choice: I found no one: as Jeremiah 5:1
decisions.reason: In Jeremiah 5:1 God tells the prophet to search Jerusalem for one person who does justice, so that he might pardon the city.

decisions.choice: {{gender:someone|a man}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word "man" here means any person, so every level has "someone" with "a man" as the alternative.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ זַעְמִ֔י בְּאֵ֥שׁ עֶבְרָתִ֖י כִּלִּיתִ֑ים דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I have poured out on them my indignation; with [the] fire of my wrath I have consumed them; their way on their heads I have brought, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: So I have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation on them; I have finished them off with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath and brought their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.31: So I have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation on them; with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath I have consumed them; I have brought their way on their heads, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.31: So I have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them. I have destroyed them with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury. I have punished them for what they have done, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I have poured out: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are past forms, but Jerusalem has not yet fallen. As often in the prophets, a coming judgment is spoken of as already done, because it is certain.

decisions.choice: I have brought their way on their heads: they bear the result of their own conduct
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 9:10, 11:21 and 16:43.

decisions.choice: I have punished them for what they have done
alternatives: I have brought their way on their heads
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m2).
